I tried both. The select-mode version feels safer and more natural to me. I like that I deliberately step into "selecting" and there's a clear "Done selecting" to step back out — it tells me I'm in a special picking state on purpose, so I'm not going to accidentally tick something while I'm just reading through my collection. The always-on checkboxes on every card felt a bit busy and a touch riskier for a fumble. Both got me from six down to four fine, but the deliberate mode is the one I'd trust. Let's go with that.

The safeguards you assumed are exactly right: I want to see how many I've got selected before I pull the trigger, and I definitely want the confirmation to spell out that this removal is permanent and can't be undone — same as the single delete. Since these are gone-for-good, that count and that explicit warning are what let me feel okay doing several at once.

One thing I want to flag for when we get there, since it's the same picking action: deleting is just one thing I might want to do to a batch. Once I've selected several, I'd also expect to be able to do other tidy-up to them together — like slap a label on all of them at once, or mark a bunch as read later — not only delete. We don't have to build that this second, but I'd want this same select mode to be where that lives.

For bulk deleting itself, though, this is what I want.
